design: Paired, prospective six-question source-grounded engineering QA. Three separate first-reader Codex participants per question, one fresh context per participant, no other-arm output, keys, coaching, inspection of the trial harness, or reruns for score.
paths: Every Python module under the two pinned nollm_core and nollm_access source trees, 44 files. Same Git blobs for every arm.

visible_budget.accounting: Meter delivered text, including repeated navigation and snippets. One common start question/instructions separately identified if outside the two evidence allowances. Identical maximum allowances; no padding or transfer of unused tokens. Answer cap applies to prose and citations together. Provider input, reasoning, cache and monetary usage are unobserved unless an actual usage record is supplied.

arms.search: A real first reader selects regex searches of the pinned sources, sees candidate paths and line numbers, then opens chosen source ranges.
arms.flat: A real first reader pages the fixed flat AOCI inventory of the same 44 modules and opens selected source ranges.
arms.surface: A real first reader chooses from actual shown native Surface previews. Only files returned by a single physical Recall may be opened. AOCI R fields are provenance text, never traversal bridges. No rerouting or lexical rescue.

geometry.field: Existing fitted 44-statement L0 field. No new atoms, coordinates, edges, bridges or layout fitting.
geometry.small_edge: 1 or 2 production samples of 96; explicitly classify absent reverse support and unequal positive reverse weights.

submission: Return an English answer and an array of at most three cited paths with line ranges read. 'Insufficient evidence' is permitted. Sources can be partially read. No external code, files or web search. Stop at the initial final submission; do not repair an answer after grading.

scoring.full: All frozen answer atoms, no material contradiction, and both required evidence roles grounded in visibly opened source and cited at supporting lines under the predeclared grading rubric.
scoring.partial: Fails full success but satisfies at least one frozen substantive atom or at least one grounded required witness.
scoring.source_metrics: Count distinct grounded cited required evidence roles, distinct opened and cited files, total required roles, missed roles, unrelated opens/citations and native candidates. Report micro precision/recall with counts and per-case outcomes.
scoring.process: Mask arm, trial directory and retrieval diagnostics before semantic grading using the frozen answer atoms and contradiction rules. Record individual votes/rationale; reconcile material disagreement against the same source, no changed gold.
scoring.cost: Per-session discovery, source, answer and returned-text token totals, source quotas, native calls, irrelevant physical returns; explicit provider usage null when unavailable.
scoring.diagnostic: Post-hoc native score and candidate support, reverse/small edges in winning paths and broader neighborhood. No outcome or diagnostic may change the questions, layout or budget.
scoring.line_anchors: An evidence role earns credit only when the same source line is present in the participant’s rendered open output, cited range and one frozen acceptable anchor; files opened via find alone cannot ground a citation. Clip ranges to actual visible source lines; ungrounded guesses cannot earn full.

allocation: One fresh Codex participant per (question, arm); counterbalance the allocation order by cyclically rotating arms across question index; use identical instructions and same inherited model configuration.
interpretation: Report paired exact counts for these six tasks. Preserve all zero/partial and transport failures. A result with this sample and one run per arm/question cannot alone establish general superiority. No merge to main.

questions.question: Design a regression test for the two paths that turn a Dream draft into a statement: ordinary Dream Formation and Dream Sculptor plan validation. Run each path twice with only the draft text edited. What should the test assert about the statement ID in each path, and which inputs explain the difference?

In one Python process a service opens a Core workspace, then tries to open the same workspace through a directory symlink. What prevents both instances from becoming mutable owners? If a later startup fails while reading malformed state, why can the service repair the file and retry in that process?

A client is parsing a wire response that confirms a provisional Field Encounter revision. Which fields belong in the wire response, how is it bound to a particular proposal, and what happens if an otherwise valid confirmation for a different proposal is supplied to an eligible, unexpired commit?

An adapter passes the complete mapping from the memory loop’s statement provenance lookup directly into the provenance record parser. Will it round-trip for both supported schema versions? How should the adapter use the returned checksum to verify and reconstruct the record?

A bridge has three distinct destination cells and max_fanout of two. A caller supplies the destinations in a preferred order that differs from their canonical order. What happens at construction, and, once the input is corrected, which two destinations can bridge-only recall follow? Can recall traverse this same bridge backwards from a destination that is outside its source anchor?

A client constructs a default-profile address at layer zero with q = r = 2**29, the default chart and no phase. It then validates that address for an active semantic write. What result should it expect at each step, and which coordinate calculation and bounds explain the difference?

answer_token_count: o200k_base of the submitted answer and citations serialized as compact UTF-8 JSON; maximum 450.
